description: Emit ordered migration plans as per-domain file-move and import-rewrite operations applied one domain at a time with atomic commits; whole-scenario big-bang apply is discouraged and guarded by analytics.

requirements.description: Cartographer must emit ordered migration plans (AC-APPLY-PLAN) as per-domain file-move and import-rewrite operations. Per-domain file moves (AC-APPLY-MOVES) and import rewrites for Go (AC-APPLY-IMPORTS-GO) must be applied one domain at a time with atomic commit-per-domain semantics (AC-APPLY-ATOMIC). Whole-scenario big-bang apply must be gated by a warning and explicit acknowledgment (AC-APPLY-WHOLE-SCENARIO-GUARD) and is strongly discouraged. Every apply operation must verify build-green status before reporting success. Migration plans must be persisted as analytics events.
requirements.title: Per-Domain Apply — Ordered Migration Plans with Atomic Commits

validation.notes: AC-APPLY-PLAN: Migration plan is emitted as an ordered list of operations (move, rewrite) per domain with no cross-domain ordering ambiguity
AC-APPLY-MOVES: File move operation updates directory structure and records the old and new paths
AC-APPLY-IMPORTS-GO: Import rewrite updates all Go import paths referencing the moved file's old package path
AC-APPLY-ATOMIC: If any operation in a domain's plan fails, all operations for that domain are rolled back
AC-APPLY-WHOLE-SCENARIO-GUARD: Invoking whole-scenario apply without --acknowledge-big-bang flag returns an error and surfaces the big-bang revert warning
Per-domain apply of a 50-file domain in bas/fixtures/medium-realistic/ completes in <10 seconds including build verification
After per-domain apply, arch-cart validate reports zero new drift conflicts for the migrated domain
Whole-scenario apply with --acknowledge-big-bang flag proceeds but logs a warning event in analytics
Atomic rollback: injecting a failure mid-plan leaves the repository in its pre-apply state
Per-domain apply (file moves + import rewrites) for a 50-file domain completes in <10 seconds including build verification
A migration performed domain-by-domain produces a clean git history with one commit per domain
The migration plan is human-readable and can be reviewed before execution

title: Per-Domain Apply
